headline: Aerobic base is proven and the taper has begun. Recent easy runs sit low and controlled. The one untouched variable — loaded, sustained-climb work — will stay untouched now.
confidence_reasons: Limited data sources active in last 3 days

sections.overview: The picture is one of a deep, consolidated base entering a deliberate wind-down with St. Olavsleden roughly two weeks out. Running over the recent block ran well above the prior four weeks, but the last handful of sessions have shortened and eased into a controlled band, which reads as intentional freshening rather than fade. Strength has held its regular cadence through the same window — the functional sessions keep ticking over without inflating systemic fatigue. Steps sit high even on rest days, so background time-on-feet remains substantial and the commute keeps adding untracked load. Recovery is the noisiest input: sleep is erratic in both duration and quality, and the cardio-load status flag reads detraining, but that flag reflects a mechanical drop in logged 7-day load against a fuller 28-day baseline — exactly what a taper produces — not a fitness loss. Read together, load is coming down on purpose while demonstrated capacity stays intact.
sections.trends: The year-to-date shape is a clear, sustained build — cumulative distance is multiples of last year at this point, and the medium-term weekly trend climbed into a genuine peak before this recent easing. That arc is coherent: a long ramp of durability and volume, now cresting into a pre-event down-slope. This isn't plateau or irregularity; it's the front edge of a taper sitting on top of a strong base, which is exactly the shape you'd want given a multi-day trail effort on the near horizon.
sections.threshold: Threshold pace remains sharp and the aerobic efficiency signal has been the throughline of the last several weeks — comparable easy efforts sitting in a lower HR band than earlier in the block. The single threshold reference point is a few weeks old now with no rolling baseline yet accumulated, so treat it as a still-valid anchor rather than a live trend. Nothing in the recent easy-run data suggests that fitness has slipped; the low HR at moderate paces is the more current and more reliable evidence, and it points to fitness being present and ready.
sections.zones: The recent runs sit predominantly in Z1–Z2 with only brief Z3 touches, which is precisely right for a taper phase — enough sustained aerobic work to hold the stimulus without accumulating fatigue. The longest recent run was almost entirely lower-zone with a large Z1 base, and the shorter runs carry only token higher-intensity minutes. There's no meaningful grey-zone drift and no session that reads as accidentally hard. The distribution matches the intent of arriving fresh: quality time-on-feet preserved, intensity deliberately clipped.
sections.hr_comparison: The strength sessions sit low and steady in HR terms — mostly Z1 with modest Z2 spillover on the longer ones — consistent with functional work that isn't spiking cardiovascular strain, so it's compatible with the taper rather than competing with it. The most recent two strength sessions logged no HR at all, which is worth noting only as a gap in the record, not a concern. Where run HR and its Polar-derived equivalents overlap, they track in the same direction and tell the same story, so effort interpretation across sessions holds together.
sections.calendar: Frequency has been dense and rhythmic through the recent block — running and strength interleaving several times a week without long gaps, which is what has built the durability now on display. As logged volume tapers, expect the calendar to thin naturally; the thing to note is that the thinning is a chosen reduction from a full pattern, not an erosion of an already-patchy one. Consistency has been the athlete's structural strength here, and it's intact right up to the wind-down.
sections.personal_bests: The short-distance and 10K bests date from a sharper, speed-oriented window last autumn and aren't the focus of this trail-and-durability block, so they're not realistically in play in the coming weeks. The relevant "best" on the horizon isn't a pace record at all — it's the multi-day effort itself, where the ultra durability being carried in will matter far more than any single-session PB.

watch_items: Watch whether the taper preserves some genuine time-on-feet rather than over-shedding into pure rest — arriving fresh, not undertrained, is the target.
Watch easy-run HR stays in its low band as volume drops; that's the cleanest confirmation the fitness is holding through the wind-down.
Watch recovery consistency as pre-event logistics ramp — sleep has been erratic, and while it doesn't drive training decisions, a run of poor nights near departure is worth simply being aware of.
